title: Wal-qadri khayrihi wa sharrihi – belief in Allah’s decree, good and bad
intro: The sixth pillar of iman: everything happens by Allah’s knowledge, decree and will.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Do you not know that Allah knows everything in the heavens and on earth? It is all in a Book – truly, that is easy for Allah. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Hajj 22:70)</small>

Belief in Allah’s decree, good or bad, is the sixth pillar of iman, which Muslims firmly believe in. Allah’s knowledge and will cover everything and are eternal. His knowledge includes what has happened to a person, what is happening now and what will happen in the future, good or bad. Every condition of a person is by Allah’s decree.

learn.title: The hadith of Jibril
learn.html: Jibril asked the Prophet (SAW) about the foundations of the Islamic faith, and he answered: “That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that you believe in the decree – both the good and the bad.” (Muslim)

Allah decreed the destiny of His creatures before He created them and wrote it in the Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet): the time of their birth, their death, their provision (rizq), their deeds, and whether they will be happy or unhappy. Nothing in the dunya can happen without Allah’s knowledge, decree and will.

learn.title: Our free choice
learn.html: Allah created people and their deeds. People really do their deeds, because Allah created in them the will and the power to do good and bad – but their will and power work within Allah’s will and power. Allah made it possible to do good and avoid bad, and showed people clearly which is which in the Qur’an’s commands and prohibitions.

A believer must believe that what is decreed – good and bad, hardship and sweetness of life – comes from Allah. When good comes, we thank Allah for His beautiful decree – that is Allah’s right over us. Whatever blessing you have is from Allah. (Qur’an, An-Nahl 16:53)

learn.text: When something we don’t like happens

items: Be patient in the test Allah sent, without despair, knowing that what reached you could not have missed you, and what missed you could not have reached you. The Prophet (SAW) said a person will not taste true iman until he knows this. (Muslim)

Be content with Allah’s decree and thank Him in every state. The Prophet (SAW) said: “How wonderful is the affair of the believer! Everything that happens to him is good – and that is only for the believer. If something good happens he is thankful and is rewarded; if something bad happens he is patient and is rewarded.” (Muslim)
Take the means: Allah also decreed the causes that can remove or change the bad. So in a test we make dua for Allah to protect us, give sadaqah and look for a cure.

learn.title: Don’t say “if only…”
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Strive for what benefits you, ask Allah for help and don’t give up. If something happens to you, don’t say: ‘If only I had done this and that’, but say: ‘This is Allah’s decree, and He does what He wills’ – because ‘if only’ opens the door to the work of Shaytan.” (Muslim)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Every condition and destiny of ours is Allah’s decree, so let’s be thankful for it, because it is surely good for us.

practice.title: Thankful or patient?
practice.prompt: What should a believer do in each case?

items.text: You got a good mark at school
You got a new baby brother
You fell ill before a trip
It rained on the day of the picnic

practice.title: In a hard test
practice.prompt: Tap what a believer does when something hard happens, then tap Check.

options.text: 😩 Says “If only I had done that…”
options.why: The Prophet (SAW) said “if only” opens the door to Shaytan. We say: “It is Allah’s decree.”

options.text: 🔮 Asks a fortune-teller about the future
options.why: Only Allah knows our destiny – fortune-telling is forbidden for Muslims.

questions.q: What is the sixth pillar of iman?
options: Belief in Allah’s decree, good and bad
Yes – Allah gave them will and power to do good or bad

questions.q: What should we say instead of “if only…”?
options: “It is Allah’s decree, and He does what He wills”

practice.title: Talk and tasks
prompts: 🤲 Talk with your muallim: thankfulness to Allah in every state, because He knows best what is good for us.
🔮 Knowledge of destiny is only with Allah, yet some people try to tell fortunes. How common is it around you, though it is forbidden for Muslims? Which kind is most common?
📝 Find and write some hadiths about Allah’s decree and the Lawh al-Mahfuz.
